No positive bypass found. A hardlink under the mechanism directory has no escaping canonical path by POSIX path semantics, but it can alias bytes from elsewhere. The gate's same-stem and mechanism-local checks constrain review semantics, not inode provenance.

adversarial_attacks.attack: real accepted-record corpus under stricter latest accepted semantics
adversarial_attacks.result: BYPASS/REJECT CONDITION: the real corpus does not normalize. The branch cannot be accepted until historical accepted records are migrated, archived, or otherwise made deliberately non-accepting without weakening the selector.

Residual ambiguity: accepted reviews require exactly one reviewer/checker object, but the code does not reject additional conflicting checker_identity or identity objects. This did not cause the observed red gate, but it is still worth closing if the schema keeps those historical containers.

Residual ambiguity: account invariant/planned-change aliases only require at least one nonempty field and are not conflict-closed. This is not a held-out selection bypass, but it can leave the causal account ambiguous.

findings.title: The follow-up gate is not landable because the real review corpus fails it
findings.evidence: The focused real-record command fails parity_review_records_are_complete at 51e06723 with accepted historical records missing explicit implementation/account/Java revisions, checker independence/tool metadata, object-shaped fresh_inputs, conflict-free evidence aliases, or canonical accounts.
findings.impact: Acceptance criterion 'Historical accepted, rejected, and pending records normalize without changing their authored verdicts' is false. The branch would make the standing evidence gate red before it can protect parity work.

findings.title: The stricter model exposes historical evidence debt but does not provide a migration boundary
findings.evidence: Latest accepted records are now judged by the new schema immediately. Many old accepted reviews are neither rejected archives nor upgraded canonical accepted reviews, so the selector clears all accepted held-outs on violations.
findings.impact: This is the right failure direction, but it needs an explicit migration strategy before integration: either upgrade records with real revisions and clean aliases, or preserve them as named rejected/pending archives so they do not claim acceptance.

findings.title: Accepted reviewer metadata is not fully conflict-closed across legacy containers
findings.evidence: validate_explicit_checker counts only reviewer/checker objects, while reviewer_objects also recognizes checker_identity and identity for historical markers. A canonical reviewer can coexist with conflicting legacy identity objects without a violation.
findings.impact: This is not the current red failure and does not by itself select bad evidence, but it leaves reviewer identity ambiguous in exactly the area this gate is meant to make unambiguous.

findings.title: Account narrative aliases are accepted by presence rather than consensus
findings.evidence: invariant/claimed_invariant and planned_change/planned_model_change are accepted if any alias is nonempty; conflicting simultaneous aliases are not rejected.
findings.impact: This does not bypass held-out selection, but it can muddy the durable causal account the gate is supposed to preserve.

residue: I did not edit product code or weaken selectors.

I did not run the full parity_perturbations product comparison because the stricter real-record gate already fails before held-outs can be selected cleanly. Prior 3d94b525's 26 divergence list remains preserved in review-rejected-3d94b525.json.
The gate itself does not verify Java commit existence in the external PlantUML repository; this review verified the configured Java revision manually.
No fresh accepted PlantUML perturbations are added for this review because the subject is the evidence gate, and the verdict is REJECT.
verdict_reason: The follow-up closes most of the prior trust-boundary holes at the unit level, but it fails the repository's actual parity_review_records_are_complete gate at head 51e06723. A red standing gate cannot be accepted as the T14 evidence normalizer. The next maker pass should migrate or deliberately de-accept historical records under the stricter model, while preserving the prior REJECT archive and without weakening selector semantics.
